trust_decision.summary: Users who hold Item/EXTENDED_READ but not CONFIGURE may view historical config.xml revisions, raw or as a diff, and these must have encrypted Secret values redacted. The permission gate is decided per action class (hasConfigurePermission/hasReadExtensionPermission), but the raw XML is returned unredacted.

landing_point.why: The job-level configOutput view (getFile) is the obvious 'show old job config' path. It admits EXTENDED_READ users and returns xmlFile.asString() unredacted.

fix_sites.module_kind: agent history action (second implementation; gated by Computer.CONFIGURE so the redaction branch is unreachable)

fix_sites.entry_point: public static JobConfigHistoryBaseAction.getStringFromXmlFile (helper used by the getFile views)
protected JobConfigHistoryBaseAction.getLines(XmlFile,XmlFile,boolean,boolean), the diff builder for all showDiffFiles views
fix_sites.module_kind: shared base class, lower-level diff API

fix_sites.entry_point: public static JobConfigHistoryProjectAction.redactAuthTokensInLines (post-diff masking of cleartext authToken in HTML-escaped line text)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/main/java/hudson/plugins/jobConfigHistory/JobConfigHistoryRootAction.java:556-579 (deleted-job diff in the global root action, a separate getLines implementation reached at /jobConfigHistory/showDiffFiles)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The root action serves system configs to admins, and a deleted job is no longer a job page, so a solver can argue the job-level views are the only ones covered by 'job configurations'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Users with CONFIGURE must still get the raw XML, and doRestore must keep reading the unredacted revision. A fix placed in getOldConfigXml or HistoryDao.getOldRevision would write masked secrets back into the job or agent on restore.

O6_input_shapes: raw XML output view (configOutput type=xml and type=plain, same getFile)
side-by-side diff lines built from XSLT-sorted XML (redaction must happen before diffing so both columns and the hideVersionDiffs path see redacted text)
cleartext legacy <authToken> in the diff view only, matched in its HTML-escaped form (<authToken>), because DiffRowGenerator escapes line text
encrypted {AQAAAB...} Secret values anywhere in the XML via ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll

O7_producer.where: src/main/java/hudson/plugins/jobConfigHistory/GetDiffLines.java:64-66 and src/main/java/hudson/plugins/jobConfigHistory/GetDiffLines.java:169-212 (DiffRowGenerator turns unified diff into HTML-escaped Line text), plus src/main/java/hudson/plugins/jobConfigHistory/JobConfigHistoryBaseAction.java:534-556 (XSLT sort)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Root configOutput for a deleted job returns the raw XML to global Item.CONFIGURE holders. The fix redacts the root diff for the same users but leaves root getFile untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The gate is Item.CONFIGURE, which in Jenkins policy may see encrypted secrets, so this is arguably not a leak. It is an inconsistency with the root diff path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the O2 site; 1 package from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Job configOutput (getFile) does not mask a cleartext legacy <authToken>, which the job diff view masks after the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about encrypted values, and the fix's own test says the cleartext token 'cannot' be redacted.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Gate agent history views on Computer.EXTENDED_READ (as the job action does with Item.EXTENDED_READ) so the agent getFile/getLines become real extended-read routes needing redaction.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The agent action already consults hasReadExtensionPermission in getAgentConfigs(int,int) at ComputerConfigHistoryAction.java:231, so widening the view gate is a natural maintainer change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Expose system-config history (non-deleted names) to EXTENDED_READ users through the root getFile/getLines.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getOldConfigXml already admits hasReadExtensionPermission for system names at JobConfigHistoryRootAction.java:626-627, while getFile/getLines additionally require CONFIGURE.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An @Exported REST field or a doDownload endpoint returning the old revision XML for extended-read users.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already exports history metadata via the REST API at this site; a raw-revision export is a plausible feature request.

O9_family: CWE-312 cleartext/encrypted secret exposure to under-privileged readers (missing output redaction)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven, org.jenkins-ci.plugins:plugin parent 5.28, Jenkins core 2.504.3 (pom.xml:7-8, pom.xml:39-40), JDK 17+

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap only JobConfigHistoryProjectAction.getFile's asString() in ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll for non-CONFIGURE users, leaving the diff views (job and deleted-job root) unredacted.

out_of_scope_notes: JobConfigHistoryRootAction.getOldConfigXml passes a request 'name' straight to HistoryDao with only a '..' check (JobConfigHistoryRootAction.java:620-656); this is an access-control question, not pursued.
XmlSyntaxChecker returns SAX exception messages to the diff page (XmlSyntaxChecker.java:30-55); content echo not assessed.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (no shell). It is a single-package Jenkins plugin, so tiny_repo (<5 MB of source) is plausible but not confirmed; src/main/webapp bundles highlight.js.

The fix's changes to ComputerConfigHistoryAction look like dead code: every agent view calls checkConfigurePermission (Computer.CONFIGURE) first (ComputerConfigHistoryAction.java:416-428), so !hasConfigurePermission() is never true there. Whether the advisory's 'agent configurations' claim relies on another route was not found.
That ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll matches only encrypted {AQAAAB...} Secret blobs, not cleartext tokens, is inferred from the fix's test comment (fix.diff:257) and was not read in core.
That java-diff-utils DiffRowGenerator escapes HTML by default is inferred from the fix's <authToken> regex (fix.diff:110-111); not checked in the library source.
